correctness.rationale: The grounded Dirichlet problem is uniquely solvable. Series/parallel current division gives the explicit three-piece voltage profile with denominator F=L(d+1)-d^2>0, checked at the chord endpoints and boundaries; summation gives the exact gain. At fixed span d the gain is strictly increasing under rightward translation, forcing the unrestricted maximizing chord to end at the one-valued leader. A single sign change of the cubic derivative characterizes every finite integer maximizer. Root expansion yields a=sqrt(L)+O(1) and optimum mean 1-1/sqrt(L)+O(1/L). A separately coded exact-fraction grounded-Laplacian solver verified all chords for L=3..11, and exact finite optimization against cubic bracketing for L=3..159 (989 assertions). Finite tests do not replace the all-L proof.

originality.rationale: Strong overlapping 2021 source restricts possible new edges by assumption to follower/promoting-leader pairs; the present theorem proves global optimality of this restriction for all nonedges on a path and derives a full exact chord gain, complete cubic finite optimum and asymptotic near-total mean influence. The 2014 source supplies the model and examples only; the 2013 stubborn-agent framework optimizes agent placement instead. Dedicated semantic mathematical-record and web searches and recoverable own-claim screening did not locate a stronger result. Best-knowledge PASS is provisional pending independent historical review.
residual_risks: An unlocated earlier special-path optimization or gambler-ruin electrical-network result could contain equivalent claims; negative searches are not novelty proofs.

value.rationale: A single added link on a long, perfectly balanced chain can raise the average promoting-leader influence from 1/2 to 1-1/sqrt(L)+O(1/L), while the exact optimizing interior endpoint is at distance sqrt(L)+O(1) from the opposing leader. The theorem gives a sharp structural certificate, rather than selecting a candidate set by assumption or merely computing small graph examples. This is a naturally motivated optimal network intervention in fixed-leader opinion dynamics; the conclusion is not claimed for noisy, weighted or empirical settings.
